body.statement: On the bounded observed-record domain \(\mathcal O\), consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap imply \(\mu_a(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Hence \(\tau(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), \(m=\mu_0+\pi\tau\), \(\lvert Y_a\rvert\le1\) almost surely, \(\lvert\mu_a\rvert\le1\), \(\lvert m\rvert\le1\), and \(\lvert\tau\rvert\le2\). Operationally, the released observed-data factors obey \(\lvert B_l(X)A Y\rvert\le K_B\), \(\lVert F_{lj}(O)\rVert_2\le K_BK_\Phi\), and \(\lVert M_j(O)\rVert_2\le K_\Phi\).
body.justification: This separates the operational privacy support restriction on observed records from its causal identification and bounded-kernel consequences.
body.gap: Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel assume a bounded observed outcome domain for private CATE learning; the present lemma records exactly how that observed-data restriction propagates through the causal model and this query.
body.consumer: It licenses the complete sensitivity ledger without assuming bounded unobserved potential outcomes as a primitive condition.
